blocks.text: Cache-first uses a stored response before trying the network. It suits files whose addresses change when their contents change.

These examples belong in separate files on your own HTTPS or localhost site. Service workers need that trusted origin and cannot run in this site's sandbox. Use browser developer tools to inspect them.

blocks.title: Choose a cache rule for a purpose

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `caches.open` opens a named Cache Storage collection. Choose versioned names that your app can manage safely.
`clone()` makes another readable response body, so storing a copy does not consume the one returned to the caller.
`response.ok` checks for a successful HTTP status. A completed fetch can still contain a 404 or another error response.

blocks.text: The helper reuses a stored response. On a first successful fetch, it saves a copy and returns the original response.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Use this only for selected safe GET assets. Personal data and frequently changing documents need a deliberate policy.
